answer: The system gives weight only to identities that lock a 200-unit insurance stake forfeited when an audit fails, so each fake funds its own stake separately. In an audit, the operator shows the ivory disc weighed at enrollment for that identity; a disc lighter by more than 0.1 gram fails. The sable cord tied across the stake box at enrollment must be uncut, and the operator must lift the box over a 2-meter trellis in one carry without setting it down. Any failure burns the 200 units and zeroes weight for 30 days, so 50 fakes risk 10,000 units.
